question: What religious practices in Judah and Jerusalem does the LORD condemn in verses 4 to 6?
The word יוֹם (yom, “day”) is repeated many times in the description of the “day of the LORD”: what portrait of this day do verses 14 to 16 build?
What does the attitude of those who say “the LORD will do nothing, good or bad” reveal, and why is it so serious?
God searches Jerusalem with lamps for the complacent: in what area of life do you risk becoming complacent before God?
What neighboring peoples are mentioned in the chapter, and in what directions do they lie from Judah?
The word עָנָו (anav, “humble”) describes those who must seek the LORD: what does seeking righteousness and humility have to do with being sheltered?
What is the sin of Moab and Ammon according to verses 8 to 10, and why does it weigh so heavily?
Nineveh said in her heart “I am, and there is none besides me”: what signs of pride like this do you notice in yourself or in your society?
What groups in Jerusalem are accused in verses 3 and 4, and with what images does the prophet describe them?
What changes are promised to the peoples and to the remnant of Israel, from “pure lips” to the tongue without deceit?
The word אַהֲבָה (ahavah, “love”) appears in the portrait of God rejoicing over His people: how does this verse change the image of God from chapter 1?
Verse 17 says God “will rejoice over you with singing”: what would your life be like if you believed this?
